A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures and supplementary material. Retained content can be matched, including v1 Figure 9 becoming v2 Figure 11.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original human-rating experiments on CLIC2020, compression comparisons, bit-allocation analyses and perceptual-metric evaluations.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by human ratings for a common-randomness ablation and additional reconstruction case studies.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain the C3 architecture, fixed common randomness, WD objective, multiscale approximation and saliency-based pooling. The variant without common randomness already appeared in v1 Figures 1 and 6.

E1.justification: Both evaluate compression on the same 41 CLIC2020 professional validation images. The additional appendix examples come from this already-evaluated dataset and introduce no new task or test environment.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds C3/WD8 without common randomness to the human-rating comparison, although this variant appeared in other analyses in v1. The external codec comparators and existing perceptual-loss baselines remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The human evaluation gains a control without common randomness. A new footnote specifies that its later-collected ratings were excluded from Table 1. The original crop-based Elo procedure and target bit rates remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 5 extends the existing common-randomness analysis with human-preference evidence. New supplementary Figures 9, 10 and 12 examine star textures, foreground detail and background-text legibility; the earlier vegetation and signage examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use 99th-percentile error bars for the rating plots and the same PCC/SRCC analysis. The new ablation follows the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no new repeated-run or statistical estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds the no-common-randomness Elo curve, showing its largest disadvantage at low bit rates. Figures 9, 10 and 12 add image-specific rates and qualitative findings. Table 1 remains unchanged, including the saliency-based WD PCC of 0.942.

T1.justification: The WD definitions, multiscale approximation and equations (1)–(4) are mathematically unchanged. No new assumptions, proofs or formal results are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the optimization-objective superiority claim from LPIPS, DISTS and MS-SSIM to LPIPS specifically, while retaining the broader rating-prediction claim. The principal quality–rate and decoding-complexity claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New Figure 12 explicitly qualifies saliency's usefulness: text legibility may not improve when the model fails to identify the text as salient. The retained signage example also receives a more cautious explanation based on assigned saliency. Existing encoding-cost and feature-selection limitations remain.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, loss-stabilization details and computational-cost information are retained. Supplementary Section 6 lists the same reconstruction archives and evaluation-data access information; no additional technical or access details accompany the new ablation.

R1.justification: The same 42 works are cited, and positioning relative to C3, COOL-CHIC and generative compression remains unchanged. Bibliographic edits abbreviate author names and venues without changing the cited research.

P1.justification: Targeted edits revise the abstract, experimental discussion, footnote and captions, update affiliations and abbreviate references. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The supplementary visual comparisons are substantially expanded and redesigned with three new multipanel figures and larger landscape presentations of retained examples. Figure 5 gains a curve and legend entry, and the quantitative plots receive typography and layout updates.

improvement.justification: The added human-rating ablation strengthens evidence for common randomness beyond v1's visual and bit-allocation analyses. The narrower abstract claim and explicit saliency failure case improve precision and qualification. These are useful, bounded gains while the method and principal quantitative conclusions remain stable.
